name: Opus 5 seasonality
strategy: Midterm-year post-election / 'best six months' seasonality book: a re-entered and smaller core SPY leg plus IWM and financials held into the historically strong Thanksgiving-through-January window, a small distillate-season refiner leg (VLO), no crypto, and 42% cash.
reassessment_note: The SPY (-8.35%) and BTC (-16.27%) stops fired as the AI/semiconductor selloff took the S&P 500 down about 8.6% in a week. News searches (WebSearch) put the cause in AI and chip stocks: the Nov 5 crash, then a multi-session losing streak on Nvidia weakness that left NVDA down more than a third from its Oct 6 high, plus software caught up in AI-agent pricing fears. Searches also said S&P earnings were still broadly strong (82% beats). I could not find a dated recap of the 11-20 session itself, so for that day I rely on the brief and the packet marks. Nothing here breaks the seasonal thesis this book was built on. The midterm-November to pre-election-year Q1 stretch is historically the strongest part of the four-year cycle, and Thanksgiving week and late December have positive base rates that have often followed a sharp early-to-mid-November washout. So I re-enter SPY at a lower price than the stop exit, at 22% instead of 30%. The stop is wider (10% vs 8%) because the stop exit itself showed that 8% is inside this tape's weekly noise. I trim IWM to 18% and keep XLF and VLO unchanged. BTC is not re-entered: it broke down with risk assets and Q4 crypto seasonality has not helped. Gross exposure falls from 74% to 58%. That cuts risk after a -9.9% drawdown without abandoning the mandate, which needs to be invested for the seasonal window to pay. Entry fills reset to the 11-23 close and all stops and take-profits are measured from there.

positions.thesis: Core seasonality leg re-entered after the 11-20 stop at about 690. The 'best six months' and midterm-to-pre-election windows run from now into Q1, and this re-entry buys them roughly 8% below the 11-13 level. Six-plus straight down sessions led by one sector (AI/semis, NVDA down more than a third), with earnings still beating, looks more like an extended positioning flush than a broad earnings recession. It is smaller than the old 30% because momentum is still negative, and the stop is 10% so ordinary aftershock volatility does not knock it out again while still capping the loss at about 2.2% of NAV.

Small caps have the strongest documented late-November-to-January seasonal (the December/January small-cap effect, including the tax-loss-selling rebound). They are also less exposed than SPY to the AI megacap unwind behind this selloff. Trimmed from 20% to 18%: the leg is down about 9% and small caps carry more beta to a growth scare. The 10% stop from the new entry caps the loss at about 1.8% of NAV.

Financials are a seasonal year-end leg (strong December and January, with buyback and dividend season into Q4 bank earnings). They have also held up better than the index in this selloff: the leg is down 5.9% vs about 8.4% for the stopped SPY leg. Held at 10%. Financials were among the worst sectors on 11-18, so the 9% stop stays as the risk cap.

Distillate-season refiner leg. Q3 2026 results showed an exceptional margin regime (net income of about $6.8B on Gulf Coast diesel cracks averaging about $72/bbl), and winter heating-oil and diesel demand keeps cracks seasonally firm into Q1. Falling crude lowers feedstock cost and does not hurt crack spreads. The risk is that cracks normalize quickly once supply returns, so this stays a small 8% leg with a 15% stop.
